why: Rotation is an index mapping: out[r][c] = matrix[n-1-c][r]. Equivalently, transpose then reverse every row; seeing both views is the whole skill.
hints: Rotate a 3x3 by hand. Where does the first row of the input end up?
The first input row becomes the last output column. Write the mapping as out[r][c] = matrix[n-1-c][r], or as transpose + reverse each row.
Build a new n x n grid with that formula (or zip(*matrix[::-1]) in Python). O(n^2) time.
pitfalls: Mixing up clockwise and counter-clockwise: check one corner. The input's bottom-left must land at the output's top-left.
For n = 1 the matrix is unchanged.
